meta.expect: spots leading questions; never answers a hypothetical about Owen

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so let's not waste it. Who decided to put a zero in the gradebook before anyone picked up a phone and called me?
I'm waiting, Hale. Owen found out from his phone in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first.
Students sometimes use tools to help with writing, yes?
You're leading me, Hale, and I've done this for twenty years. I'm not answering a hypothetical about my son. You still haven't told me who decided on that zero.
And Owen was stressed in October, with work and everything?
That's twice now, and Owen's job and his schedule are none of your business. Do you have anything with a date on it, or am I walking to the principal's office?
So it's at least possible he used it once?
"Possible." I'm writing down that your case against my son is "possible," and that you've led me three times without showing me a single page. Show me something, Hale, or this goes upstairs today.
No. I agree you've used that word twice, Hale, and that's all you've got.
